knownFindings.reason: Physical non-solid admission uses actual particle cubes and compact pair lenses, not nominal-bin occupancy. All original 34 controls pass unchanged, with neutral/swimming and existing vertical support preserved. New geometric/force controls cover compact support and numerical tangency. This is bounded sampling reconstruction, not exact multiphase topology or a conserved-volume solve. See docs/FLUID_LOCAL_WET_RECONSTRUCTION.txt.

Analytic nonplanar geometry exposes error in both legacy PBF wet-volume reconstruction and the original remote-plane observer. Strict diagnostic stays failing; Advanced Fluids remain locked. See docs/FLUID_KNOWN_GEOMETRY_COMPARISON.md.
Pass2 finite swept-SAT bounds correct the validated first-arrival contract; it now runs in the ordinary collision group. This does not close later curved-sheet continuation.
Original unchanged mesh arrival/continuation fixtures pass with authoritative MK2. Bounded CCD, sidedness and deep initial-overlap limits remain; MK1 event scheduling has been removed.

Legacy PBF remains locked in Alpha. The accumulated-motion epoch repair passes production acceptance windows and all five original four-second comparisons; original failed evidence is preserved. Two production and four player warm-up diagnostics still fail, and coarse impact/contact transients and geometric limitations remain. Active particle continuation/suspension/origin shifts are still unsupported. See docs/FLUID_MOTION_CLOCK_REPAIR.txt.
Original a106 snapshot lacks historical continuation data. New-format passes do not certify that snapshot.
Original MK1 global event cascade is retired. Current MK2 measurements have their own workload scope; focused correctness gates do not certify universal dense-pile latency.

Baker and runtime use the same normalized owner/field frames and oriented gravity volumes; both original bake-only runtime-publication cases pass unchanged equivalence tolerances. Original full integration exposes separate retained exact-total comparison failure.

Positive tetrahedral density is integrated into one monotone cumulative curve, including shared endpoints; unchanged strict Surface1 decoder accepts both original rotated bakes. A later origin sampling limitation remains separately failed.

The original half-turn fixture now bakes and publishes, then fails its unchanged post-512m-origin query comparison: float translation crosses a discontinuous disturbed-surface cell boundary. Conserved quantities and wave bytes remain unchanged. This full integration failure is preserved, not counted as a baking pass.

Pass3 preserves the original failed test and demonstrates its causal-baseline error. Current atomicity compares the immediate pre-request total with the same exact equality and every physical participant byte; earlier legitimate paired-flow conservation tolerance and liquid runtime are unchanged.
